test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is meant by non-biodegradable?

options.text: Substances that are broken down by biological processes
Substances that are not broken down by biological processes
Substances that are broken down by biochemical reactions.
Substances that are not broken down by chemical processes

solution:
The correct answer is __**Substances that are not broken down by biological processes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Non-biodegradable substances** are materials that cannot be decomposed by natural biological processes.
 
• These substances tend to persist in the environment for a long time, often causing pollution.
 
• Common examples include plastics, synthetic chemicals, and certain types of metals.
 
• Managing non-biodegradable waste is crucial for environmental protection and sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodegradable Substances:**

 
 
• These are materials that can be broken down by microorganisms into simpler, non-toxic substances.
 
• Common examples include food scraps, paper, and natural fibers like cotton and wool.
 
• Biodegradation is a crucial process in the natural recycling of organic matter.
 
• Proper waste management of biodegradable substances helps reduce landfill use and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Non-Biodegradable Substances:**
 
 
• Non-biodegradable waste contributes significantly to environmental pollution.
 
• Plastics, in particular, can cause harm to wildlife and marine life.
 
• These substances often accumulate in landfills, leading to soil and water contamination.
 
• Efforts to reduce the use of non-biodegradable materials include recycling, using alternative materials, and promoting sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Recycling and Waste Management:**
 
 
• Recycling is the process of converting waste materials into new materials and objects.
 
• Effective waste management involves reducing, reusing, and recycling materials to minimize environmental impact.
 
• Governments and organizations are increasingly promoting recycling programs to manage non-biodegradable waste effectively.
 
• Public awareness and participation are essential for the success of recycling and waste management initiatives.
